chunks: Saffan narrated from Abu al-Maghra' who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the person in Ihram washing his hand with ash (potash). He (peace be upon him) said: 'My father used to wash his hand with white ash (potash).'

key_terms.الْأَبْيَضِ: White (specifying the type of potash used)
key_terms.الْأُشْنَانِ: Potash or ash used for washing/cleaning
key_terms.الْحُرُضِ: A specific type of potash or ash, often implying a purer or finer variety
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of Ihram (consecration for pilgrimage)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a person in Ihram to wash their hands with potash (ash)?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the permissibility of using scented substances for washing in Ihram, distinguishing between the prohibition of wearing scented clothing and the allowance of using scents for hygiene. It highlights the scholarly tradition of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) by referencing the specific practice of his father, Imam al-Baqir (AS), who used white *hurud* (a type of potash or soap), thereby establishing a precedent for using aromatic agents during the state of consecration.
